learning.title: A gate that walks branch commits can fail on a commit you checked past
learning.trigger: Debugging a gate that reports a stale or mismatched digest (paper parity K-0, contract compatibility digests, any provenance check) when the artifact "obviously" matches, especially after a rebase, squash or amend.
learning.mistake: Verified the endpoints — origin/main and the current branch tip — found both clean, and concluded the gate was wrong or the failure was pre-existing. The gate in fact iterated every snapshot in the branch's history, and an intermediate commit (a pre-rebase commit still reachable after a reword-only rebase) carried the bad digest. Endpoints agreeing says nothing about the commits between them.
learning.rule: Read the gate's snapshot enumeration before reproducing. `snapshotAt(commit)` in compare-paper.mjs reads a specific commit, not the worktree; a rebase that only rewords or reorders keeps old commits reachable, so a bad one survives. Enumerate `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` and test each commit's artifact, not just the tip. Reproduce with the gate's own arguments — its default parameters, its own `read`, its own helper imports — because a hand-written reproduction that differs in one default (a wrong module path for launch options, a wrong repository root) will "disprove" a correct gate.

Distinguish "pre-existing on main" from "mine" by stashing and re-running at the base, not by reading the diff. If the count and the message are identical with your work stashed, it is pre-existing; if the message names a commit that is an ancestor of your branch, it is yours.

verification.requirement: Every commit in the branch range must pass the gate's own check before the failure is called external.
A failure is only called pre-existing when the identical count and message reproduce with the branch's changes stashed at the base.

learning.boundary: The squash that fixes this is legitimate only once the offending commit is identified and the removal understood; squashing to silence an unexplained gate is the failure mode this rule exists to prevent.
